page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a running head at the top centre. Section titles are centred in spaced capitals. No page number, catchword or signature. A printed ornament band sits at the foot and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: 37. An Prandiū Cœnâ liberalius esse debeat? Italus quidam 2.prop.libris.

p.i: Nos sanis corporibus id liberum relinquimus.

main_text.p: 38. Utrum quis assuefieri possit, ut venena inno-cuè sumat?
39. Vinum quoq; an hystericis Mulieribus com-petat? Lis inter Hippocr. & Avicenn. D.Lang. epist. t. 1. num. 23.
40. Nutricibus quoq; vini usus an conferat?
main_text.head: PHARMACEUTICA.
CHIRURGICA.
main_text.p: 42. An Corpori alimentum per Clysteria sup-peditari possit? Avenzoar nobilis Arabs suæ Med.l.1. tract.10. c.18.
main_text.head: SEMEIOTICA.
main_text.p: 43. Ex Urinis morborum vaticinium utrum sit temerarium? Doct. Fuchs. in Instit.
44. An Sudor plus quàm Urina de humoribus indicet? Hippocr. apud Lang.
45. Utrum Somnia quoq; Medicis sint obser-vanda? Mira apud Galen.
main_text.head: COS INGENIORUM THEOREMATA.

page.notes: The question numbers 37 to 45 stand at the start of each paragraph inside the text block, not in a margin. The printed ornament band at the foot is decoration and is left out. Long s is written as plain s. "Instit." in no. 43 is read from a small, slightly worn form and may be "Institit." or "Instit.". The macron on "Prandiū" and "Medicamentū" and the grave accent on "cuè" and "quàm" are read from the print and may be less certain at this resolution. The printed line "Nos sanis" is read as a separate indented paragraph.
